Director Terms
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next annual meeting and until the election and qualification of their successor, or their earlier death, resignation, or removal.

Management
Director Terms
Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time, each of our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires.

Management
Director Terms
As a result, only one class of directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual meeting of stockholders following their election and until his or her successor has been elected and qualified, or until his or her earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of onethird of our directors.
Regardless of the class or classes of stock by which a director is elected, there is no limit to the number of terms a director may serve.

Executive Summary
At Anthropic, we strive to build a team that is aligned with our mission and values. Executive compensation reflects our overall compensation philosophy, which prioritizes competitive pay that targets the 90th percentile of the AI development market, consistent pay for the same role, level, and location, and simplicity of plan design. In 2025, we offered a competitive mix of base salary, long-term equity incentive awards (including stock options and RSUs), and other benefits to attract and retain top talent in a competitive market environment.

Executive Summary
Compensation Philosophy and Objectives
Our executive compensation philosophy is to provide our executive officers with consistent cash and equity compensation for the same role, level, and location. When determining executive compensation, we review each executive’s current compensation against role- and level-specific market data. We do this bi-annually as part of our performance and compensation cycle where we review proposed market-based and promotion-based cash and equity increases for executives. We plan to continue to regularly review, and potentially adjust, our executive compensation programs to ensure they are consistent with our compensation philosophy as a public company.

Other Compensation Governance Practices
Compensation Recovery Policy
We have adopted an executive compensation recoupment policy intended to comply with the requirements of Rule 10D-1 under the Exchange Act and the rules of the stock exchange on which our securities are listed (“Clawback Policy”) that will be effective upon the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part. The Clawback Policy will generally require us to recover erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation that was received by covered executive officers in the event we are required to prepare an accounting restatement due to any material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the securities laws (including any required accounting restatement to correct an error in previously issued financial statements that is material to the previously issued financial statements), or that would result in a material misstatement if the error were corrected in the current period or left uncorrected in the current period.

Executive Compensation
Other Compensation Governance Practices
Compensation Recovery Policy
The Clawback Policy generally covers incentive-based compensation received on or after the effective date of the Clawback Policy and during the three-year period prior to the date we are required to prepare the financial restatement. The amount required to be recovered is the excess of the amount of incentive-based compensation received over the amount that otherwise would have been received based on the restated financial measure.

Executive Compensation
Other Compensation Governance Practices
Hedging, Pledging, and Insider Trading
We are dedicated to fostering high standards of ethical business conduct and adherence to applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Accordingly, we maintain our Insider Trading Policy, which we believe is appropriately designed to foster compliance with insider trading laws, rules, and regulations, and the listing standards of the Nasdaq Global Select Market that will be applicable to us. Our Insider Trading Policy applies to all of our officers, directors, and employees, as well as designated consultants, and specifically prohibits ownership of financial instruments or participation in investment strategies that hedge the economic risk of owning our equity securities, such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, and collars.

Executive Compensation
Other Compensation Governance Practices
Hedging, Pledging, and Insider Trading
Directors, officers, and other employees are prohibited from maintaining company securities in a margin account or otherwise pledging company securities as collateral for a loan, provided that certain limited exceptions may be permitted. In addition, we prohibit our executive officers, directors, and employees from purchasing or selling our securities while in possession of material, non-public information or otherwise utilizing such information for their personal benefit. We maintain a quarterly blackout window where applicable individuals may not trade.

Policies and Practices Related to the Grant of Certain Equity Awards Close in Time to the Release of Material Nonpublic Information
We periodically grant stock options to our NEOs, employees, and other service providers. We have historically granted options on or shortly after a newly hired employee’s start date. We have historically granted refresh, promotion, or market adjustment options when and as determined by our board of directors. We have no specific policy or practice regarding the timing of options or other equity grants in relation to the public disclosure of material nonpublic information by the company.

Tax and Accounting Considerations
Tax Considerations
Section 162(m) of the Code imposes a $1 million limit on the amount of compensation that we may deduct as a business expense in any year with regard to certain of our most highly paid executive officers. While our board of directors considers the deductibility of compensation as one factor in determining executive compensation, our board of directors retains the discretion to award compensation that is not deductible as it believes that it is in our best interests to maintain flexibility in our approach to executive compensation in order to design a program that we deem to be the most effective in attracting, motivating, and retaining key executives and aligning pay with performance.

Executive Compensation
Tax and Accounting Considerations
Accounting Considerations
Our board of directors takes accounting considerations into account in designing compensation plans and arrangements for our NEOs and other employees. We follow the Financial Accounting Standards Board’s Accounting Standards Codification Topic 718 (“FASB ASC Topic 718”) for our stock-based compensation awards. FASB ASC Topic 718 requires us to measure the compensation expense for all share-based payment awards based on the grant date “fair value” of these awards.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
We have four classes of authorized common stock:
• the class designated as Participating Common Stock, which is divided into two series: Class A common stock and Class N common stock;
• Class T common stock, which is a special class of common stock that is issued to the LTBT;
• Class F common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to the Founder LLC; and
• Class E common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to our employees, excluding our co-founders.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Voting Rights
• Class A common stock. Holders of our Class A common stock are entitled to one vote for each share held on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors.
• Class N common stock. Holders of our Class N common stock are not entitled to vote on any matter that is submitted to a vote of stockholders, except as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class N common stock without so adversely affecting our Class A common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a series.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Voting Rights
• Class T common stock. The holder of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors, the redemption of our Class E common stock, certain amendments to the rights of our Class F common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class T common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Voting Rights
• Class F common stock. The holder of our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date on matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will be voted in the manner provided by the Founder LLC Agreement. See the section titled “—Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.”

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Voting Rights
• Class E common stock. The holders of our Class E common stock have no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the proposed nomination, removal, or change in designation of the Specified Class T Director (in circumstances where our NGC does not concur with the LTBT’s proposed action), certain changes to the terms of the LTBT, the rights of our Class T common stock, the redemption of our Class T common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class E common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Conversion and Transferability
• Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the section titled “Shares Eligible for Future Sale—Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class A common stock can be transferred.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Conversion and Transferability
• Class N common stock. The holders of our Class N common stock are primarily strategic business partners. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the section titled “Shares Eligible for Future Sale—Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class N common stock can be transferred. The shares of Class N common stock will automatically convert into an equal number of shares of Class A common stock upon a transfer effected through: (i) a registered offering or an open market sale of such shares or (ii) a transfer to a third party (A) that is not a holder of Class N common stock (or an affiliate of a holder of Class N common stock) and (B) that will not beneficially own or control more than 9.99% of the shares of any class or series of our equity securities after giving effect to the transfer.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Conversion and Transferability
• Class T common stock. Our Class T common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Our Class T common stock is transferable only upon the approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. Because the persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold have the power to modify or terminate the LTBT and the rights of our Class T common stock entirely, there is no separate restriction on the identity of a permissible transferee of our Class T common stock.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Conversion and Transferability
• Class F common stock. Our Class F common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Our Class F common stock is not transferable except in the case of a reorganization or redomiciliation of the Founder LLC that is approved by our board of directors and does not result in a change to the members of the Founder LLC.
• Class E common stock. Our Class E common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock and is not transferable.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Redemption
• Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be redeemable at our option or at the option of the holder.
• Class N common stock. Our Class N common stock will not be redeemable at our option or at the option of the holder.
• Class T common stock. Our Class T common stock will be redeemable for no consideration:
◦ if the Trustees are voting in favor of such redemption, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up));
◦ if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such redemption:

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Redemption
• at any time, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or
◦ if no Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such redemption, upon approval of 85% of the outstanding shares of Class A common stock.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Redemption
• Class F common stock. Our Class F common stock will be redeemable for no consideration (i) at the option of the Founder LLC, acting upon Supermajority approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, or (iii) upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, which will commence when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Redemption
• Class E common stock. Our Class E common stock will not be redeemable at the option of the holder. Following an employee’s separation from employment with us other than for cause, one-half of such employee’s then-outstanding shares of Class E common stock will be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration annually, except that all shares of Class E common stock held by an employee will also be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration upon such employee’s death, incapacity, termination for cause, or commencement of service with a direct competitor. All shares of Class E common stock will also be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration (i) at such time as no Class F common stock remains outstanding, or (ii) upon the approval of (A) 80% of authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)), (B) the holder of our Class F common stock, and (C) the holder of our Class T common stock.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Dividend Rights
Subject to preferences that may apply to any shares of preferred stock outstanding at the time, the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock are entitled to receive dividends out of funds legally available if our board of directors, in its discretion, determines to issue dividends and then only at the times and in the amounts that our board of directors may determine. Our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock are not entitled to receive dividends. See the section titled “Dividend Policy” for more information.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
No Preemptive or Similar Rights
Our common stock is not entitled to preemptive rights and is not subject to redemption or sinking fund provisions (other than those providing for the redemption of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock for no consideration described above).

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Right to Receive Liquidation Distributions
If we become subject to a liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up, the assets legally available for distribution to our stockholders would be distributable ratably among the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock and any participating preferred stock outstanding at that time, subject to prior satisfaction of all outstanding debt and liabilities and the preferential rights of and the payment of liquidation preferences, if any, on any outstanding shares of our capital stock. In the event of our liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up, holders of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock shall be entitled to receive par value ($0.00001) per share but shall not otherwise participate in such distributions.

Description of Capital Stock
Common Stock
Fully Paid and Non-Assessable
In connection with this offering, our legal counsel will opine that the shares of our Class A common stock to be issued in this offering will be fully paid and non-assessable.

Underwriting
Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements
In order to facilitate the offering of our Class A common stock, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, acting as stabilization agent on behalf of the underwriters, may engage in transactions that stabilize, maintain, or otherwise affect the price of our Class A common stock. Specifically, the underwriter may sell more shares of Class A common stock than the underwriters are obligated to purchase under the underwriting agreement, creating a short position. A short sale is covered if the short position is no greater than the number of shares available for purchase under the over-allotment option. The underwriter can close out a covered short sale by exercising the over-allotment option or purchasing shares in the open market.

Underwriting
Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements
In determining the source of shares to close out a covered short sale, the underwriter will consider, among other things, the open market price of our Class A common stock compared to the price available under the over-allotment option. The underwriter may also sell shares of Class A common stock in excess of the over-allotment option, creating a naked short position. The underwriter must close out any naked short position by purchasing shares of Class A common stock in the open market. A naked short position is more likely to be created if the underwriter is concerned that there may be downward pressure on the price of our Class A common stock in the open market after pricing that could adversely affect investors who purchase shares of Class A common stock in this offering.

Fair Value of Convertible Notes Description The Company accounts for its convertible promissory notes at fair value. As discussed in of the Note 4 to the consolidated financial statements, the estimated fair value of convertible Matter promissory notes as of December 31, 2025, was $41.7 billion and the recognized loss for the change in the fair value of the convertible promissory notes for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $34.5 billion. The Company estimated the fair value of the convertible promissory notes using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis method and a common stock equivalent method which involved the use of complex and subjective estimates, judgments and assumptions.

The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is particularly sensitive to changes in the relative weight applied to the two valuation methods.

Fair Value Measurements and Financial Instruments
Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. In accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 820, Fair Value Measurement (“ASC 820”), the Company uses the fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value. The hierarchy, as defined below, gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are set forth below:

Report Of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
1. Description of Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
Fair Value Measurements and Financial Instruments
Level 1: Observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
Level 2: Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are not active or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly for the full term of the assets or liabilities.
Level 3: Unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities.

Evaluation of Long-Lived Assets for Impairment
Long-lived assets, such as property and equipment, right-of-use (“ROU”) assets, and finite-lived intangible assets subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset or asset group (collectively, the “asset group”) may not be recoverable. The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for income taxes. 4. Fair Value Measurements
The SAFE liabilities are recorded at fair value, which is determined based on a third-party valuation utilizing a scenario-based analysis and a CCA, that considers specific scenarios that factor in timing, probability, and financing size. This model takes into account the contract terms as well as multiple inputs, such as the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock price, risk free interest rates, and expected volatility, some of which the Company could not corroborate with observable market data. The assumptions used in valuing the SAFE liability upon conversion on December 31, 2023 and on January 30, 2024, include volatility, risk free interest rate, and term to liquidity. Changes in the fair value measurement of the SAFE liabilities relate to the conversion scenarios and are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations. All SAFEs have been converted as of December 31, 2024.

Report Of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
4. Fair Value Measurements
The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a CCA and a CSE method. The analysis estimates the fair value of the convertible notes based on the probabilityweighted expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock, and maturity. Assumptions include weight applied to the CCA and CSE methods, assumed volatility, time to a liquidity event, need for and terms of financings or expected financings, and the risk free interest rate. Changes in fair value of the convertible notes are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations.

SAFEs
The Company determined that the SAFEs are not legal form debt (i.e., no creditors’ rights). The monetary settlement amount of the SAFEs is based upon a fixed or determinable amount known at inception, and the number of equity shares received upon conversion is variable. In such circumstances, equity classification is not appropriate because such contracts that are settled based upon a fixed amount do not expose the holder to risks and rewards similar to those of an equity-holder, therefore, the SAFEs would have been classified as marked-tomarket liabilities pursuant to ASC 480.

Section 145 of the DGCL authorizes a corporation’s board of directors to grant, and authorizes a court to award, indemnity to officers, directors, and other corporate agents.
We expect to adopt an amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, and which will contain provisions that limit the liability of our directors and certain officers for monetary damages to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law. Consequently, neither our directors nor certain officers will be personally liable to us or our stockholders for monetary damages for any breach of fiduciary duties as directors or officers, as applicable, except liability for the following:
• any breach of the director’s or officer’s duty of loyalty to our company or our stockholders;

Part II

• any act or omission not in good faith or that involves intentional misconduct or a knowing violation of law;
• for our directors, unlawful payments of dividends or unlawful stock repurchases or redemptions as provided in Section 174 of the DGCL;
• any transaction from which the director or officer derived an improper personal benefit; or
• for our officers, any action by or in the right of the corporation.
Any amendment to, or repeal of, these provisions will not eliminate or reduce the effect of these provisions in respect of any act, omission, or claim that occurred or arose prior to that amendment or repeal. If the DGCL is amended to provide for further limitations on the personal liability of directors or officers of corporations, then the personal liability of our directors and officers will be further limited to the greatest extent permitted by the DGCL.
